scope: Connected original published global proc/sys resource subsystem: traversal and metadata refresh, ordinary/FileWork reads, existing read-only namespace rejection, fixed/linked io_uring, original OFD/publication lifetime, close/reuse, completion and cancellation.

architecture.publication: Private legacy query projections retain the original synchronized global publication. Projection capture is flattened to the same root; there is no copied owner VFS or Files authority.
architecture.files: Opened descriptions retain the original global publication through the existing type-erased ProcSource boundary and common FileWork. Numeric PID/mm payloads retain their real typed capability checks.
architecture.updates: Later publications and a subsequently bound live provider remain visible. Provider callbacks run outside the publication lock. Root/global data, weak open/PID bindings and original UTS/network/cgroup resources are retained without a Files-root cycle.
architecture.lifetime: Retained file work survives original owner/table close and releases the global root after last accepted description. io_uring links and registrations retain the original OFD across FD reuse; the original submitter owns copyout/cancellation.
no_new: production unsafe trait implementation or block

validation_notes: The new connected process fixture fails against the prior runtime at pread, before its completion marker. Final four/twelve-CPU, one-slot and seccomp ALLOW cases finish pread plus a fixed-file io_uring request in one cohort with zero returned syscall, service or mapping checkpoint.

The signed native prior four-CPU workload completes functionally but needs five cohorts, four returned preads and two returned clones. Final four/twelve-CPU workloads use one cohort with no returned syscall or service; per-thread data and actual CQEs are verified. No twelve-CPU before measurement or throughput speedup is claimed.

The linked io_uring fixture retains a global metadata OFD across close/reuse, reads a later publication after its eventfd dependency completes, keeps another submitter running and tests cancellation without copyout. Cancellation CQE order follows existing concurrency semantics; the test compares the completion set.

Global metadata now supports source namespace/metadata lookup and canonical read-only EROFS rejection. Earlier tests that blanket-excluded /sys or /proc are split into positive published-resource checks and explicit provider-unavailable negative checks, preserving original errors and before-effects assertions.

The dormant native fixture uses a readable original global OFD opened with an explicitly unavailable source provider, rather than a fake errno. Both old/final runtimes keep its real setup join and subsequent cold-wake coverage.

During construction, a concrete enum reference to PseudoFs exceeded an existing auto-trait solver depth in a dependent test. The final original publication provider uses the existing type-erased ProcSource boundary and passes strict lint with no new unsafe Send/Sync implementation or increased recursion limit.

The new fixed-file process test initially called the Kernel-only syscall helper for io_uring_register; its final setup uses the real Linux ABI dispatch. A test-only Duration import and capability/traversal fixture expectations were corrected before final checks.

Final changed Rust fingerprints match ARM Linux CI and the paired Mac checkout. Complete runtime workflows and Mac development gates 1-8 of 12 pass; stable packaging and physical iPad installation are outside this round.
